entitySubtype: Scientific Preprint / Infrared Photometry and Kinematic Interpretation
name: Six objects reported at 480 mph in a declassified military infrared video show brightness flicker at bird wingbeat rates
summary: Scientific preprint applying frame-by-frame photometry, control tests, Galileo Project animal comparisons and parallax modeling to DOW-UAP-PR135. The authors report independent 7.1–7.9 Hz brightness fluctuations and propose a nearby flock of birds as the best explanation, while identifying unredacted telemetry as capable of testing or refuting the hypothesis.

publicationMetadata.publicationStatus: Scientific preprint submitted to Scientific Reports; peer review and acceptance not established

researchLibraryMetadata.methodology: Measures frame-by-frame brightness for all six PR135 objects, tests constant-brightness control targets for sensor/compression artifacts, compares periodicity with Galileo Project infrared recordings of flying animals, and models the viewing geometry needed to reproduce the reported projected speed.
researchLibraryMetadata.dataset: DOW-UAP-PR135 plus comparison recordings from Galileo Project ground-based infrared cameras near Las Vegas.
researchLibraryMetadata.principalFindings: The six objects show independent 7.1–7.9 Hz brightness periodicity; the comparison animal data span approximately 3.4–10.0 Hz; and a nearby slow-moving geometry can reproduce the reported projected motion.
researchLibraryMetadata.limitations: The public video lacks unredacted sensor and platform telemetry needed to determine actual range, altitude and physical velocity or to conclusively identify the objects.
researchLibraryMetadata.researchImplication: The bird-and-parallax model is a reproducible, testable conventional explanation, not a definitive identification.

evidenceRecords.label: Six PR135 brightness time series
evidenceRecords.finding: Each tracked object exhibits its own periodic 7.1–7.9 Hz brightness variation.

evidenceRecords.label: Constant-brightness control targets
evidenceRecords.finding: Tested sensor/compression processing did not reproduce the periodic signal.

evidenceRecords.label: Galileo Project flying-animal comparison
evidenceRecords.finding: Infrared animal periodicities overlap the PR135 frequency range.

evidenceRecords.label: PR135 parallax geometry
evidenceRecords.finding: A nearby slow-moving object can produce the reported ground-projected motion under the modeled geometry.

editorialNotes.neutrality: The paper authors favor birds; GreyAlien does not convert that provisional preprint interpretation into an official or definitive identification.
editorialNotes.speedDiscipline: Approximately 480 mph remains a mission-report ground-projected estimate, not independently recovered object airspeed.
editorialNotes.comparisonDiscipline: Frequency overlap supports comparison but does not establish species identity.
editorialNotes.lifecyclePrinciple: News can age; knowledge does not.
